Building Autonomous Agents with Apollia OS

By Jane Doe · April 14, 2026

Apollia OS is an open-source Rust runtime designed to run AI agents locally on your own machine. Unlike cloud-hosted agent platforms, Apollia gives you complete control over how agents execute, what data they can access, and where that data lives. This article walks through a complete example of building an agent that performs weekly competitive intelligence: it searches the web, reads articles, synthesises the findings, and stores the result in its private memory.

Why Local-first Matters

Running agents locally has three practical advantages. First, you never pay per-token fees for a cloud agent platform on top of the LLM costs you already pay. Second, your queries never leave your machine unless you explicitly allow it. Third, agents can touch files, run shell commands, and hit APIs with local credentials that would be awkward to pass to a hosted service.

The Agent Loop

Apollia implements a minimal ReAct loop: Observe, Reason, Act. The runtime enforces a step budget to guarantee termination, and every tool call is audited in a SQLite journal. The agent itself is just a Python function with an async run() method and a manifest declaring which tools it needs.

This design keeps the integration surface tiny: duck-typing at the Python boundary, and a strict sandbox enforced by the Rust runtime at every tool invocation. New agents can be prototyped in minutes without modifying the core runtime.

A Concrete Example

Our competitive-intelligence agent uses three native tools: web_search (pluggable backends, default DuckDuckGo), web_read (fetches a URL and returns readable text), and memory_store (namespaced SQLite with FTS5). The full manifest is under 30 lines of Python.
